report:
All 5 segments (Sanjac_Rec_91 0124–0140) are labelled and accepted on the first submit, with 0 rejected. `label get attributes --rec Sanjac_Rec_91` shows all 5 stored. The other 9 segments stored for this recording come from other jobs.

| Segment | Persons in corridor | Positive attributes | Turn (max excursion) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0124 | ONE_TWO | stationary group (women handing out items to the right of the path) | no (10.5°) |
| 0128 | ONE_TWO | vehicle present left as TRUTH_UNKNOWN | yes (52°) |
| 0132 | ZERO | vehicle present (utility cart, lidar puts it about 15 m away) | no (25.6°) |
| 0136 | ZERO | vehicle present (pickup, about 16 m) | yes (32.7°) |
| 0140 | ONE_TWO | none | yes (166.7°) |

**Borderline calls:**
- **0128, `vehicle_present` = TRUTH_UNKNOWN.** A white utility cart is visible at 127.9 s. Lidar places it at about 15.5 m at 130.0 s, which works back to roughly 19–20 m at the end of the segment. That sits right on the 20 m limit, so I didn't call it either way.
- **0140, persons = ONE_TWO.** Three men walk toward the robot at about 4–5 m (frame #4157, lidar #1373). Only the one in the orange polo looks clearly inside the 1.5 m corridor; the other two are about 1.1–1.3 m to the right. If the corridor edge is judged more generously this becomes THREE_FIVE.
- **0132 and 0136, `vehicle_interaction` = FALSE.** The vehicles cross or drive away at about 15 m or more, outside the 10 m rule.

**Tool friction:**
1. **`step` is too short on the Jackal.** `--n 4` gives 4 frames about 33 ms apart (0.1 s in total), which is useless for seeing people enter or leave view. It needs a `--stride`/`--dt` option, or should default to about 0.5 s spacing.
2. **No distance for things beyond 5 m.** Every `vehicle_present` call depended on the ~20 m rule, and I had to estimate range by hand: match a lidar blob to the camera bearing, then count rings at 12–15 px per metre. A range-and-bearing readout or a click-to-measure would help, and so would marking which lidar clusters fall inside the front camera's field of view.
3. **The `min_range_corridor_m` signal picks up curbs and walls.** The dips at about 128.2 s and 137.9 s were a curb wall and a planter, not people, so the signal can't be read as "a person in the path" without checking the camera each time.
4. **Shell restrictions.** `for` loops (`$s`), `export`, and some `grep` patterns are blocked, so each command has to be written out in full with the `SCANDQ_JOB=` prefix. A `scandq window` that accepts several segments at once, or a `--summary` flag that prints only path, heading and odom refs, would save a lot of calls.
5. **Glare.** Lens flare at about 131–132 s turns the pickup red and partly hides it. This is only minor.
